entries.name: Generic destroy operator contract
entries.description: Domain-defined partial destruction over an owned incumbent clone with explicit destruction-size input.
entries.formula: The destroy operator maps a complete incumbent clone to a domain-owned partial representation and removed-component token; no partial objective is evaluated.

entries.name: Generic repair operator contract
entries.description: Domain-defined reconstruction that restores a complete evaluable candidate.
entries.formula: The repair operator consumes the partial representation and removed-component token and must restore a complete candidate before common objective evaluation.

entries.name: Strict-improvement incumbent acceptance
entries.description: Canonical local-search acceptance that replaces the incumbent only on strict objective improvement.

entries.name: Shaw related-customer removal
entries.description: Routing-specific relatedness combines structural proximity information and belongs to the domain model.
entries.formula: The exact relatedness metric depends on routing-specific distance, timing and request attributes and is therefore not universalized by the generic core.

entries.name: Constraint-based reinsertion with Limited Discrepancy Search
entries.description: Original Shaw reconstruction uses constraint-based tree search with Limited Discrepancy Search.
entries.formula: Faithful implementation requires a first-class constraint-search model and discrepancy semantics rather than a generic repair flag.

entries.name: Adaptive destroy/repair operator selection
entries.description: Competing destroy and repair subheuristics are selected by the separate public ALNS controller introduced in v0.53. The mechanism remains outside the canonical Shaw LNS identity.
entries.formula: Adaptive operator selection is implemented separately by stable ID adaptive-large-neighborhood-search-ropke-pisinger-2006 and is not folded into the canonical LNS identity.

references.publication: Pisinger & Ropke (2010), Large Neighborhood Search overview
Ropke & Pisinger (2006), Adaptive Large Neighborhood Search
